utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-94-2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry we are late. I'm afraid I was involved in some other matter, but the transcript I hope will be corrected to show that we are not starting at five past 1.00 but at five past 10.00. This is the Status Conference required under the rules. Is there anything that the Prosecution wants to raise, Mr. Ryneveld?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Not that I can think of this morning. Thank you, Your Honour. The only thing that had occurred to me is perhaps the court at some point may wish to order a date to disclose names to the Defence, but I don't know whether this is an appropriate time or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that depends on when the trial is, and I think we have a long way ahead of us before that by the look of this motion. But what is happening about the form of the indictment with the 80 counts?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can tell the Court that we are in the process of actually working on preparing an amended indictment, and I can assure the court that when I'm done with it, it will be substantially reduced. I'm not in a position yet to file the amended indictment. There have been some other matters that have been requiring my immediate attention. However, I am in the process of reviewing with our staff the amended indictment, and I anticipate, as I say, it will probably be less than half of the amount of counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I should hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to the matters requiring your immediate attention, may I point out that we are still waiting for some material in that other case and that my power to deal with the matter will shortly expire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm acutely aware of that, Your Honour, and as we speak, those matters are being attended to, and I understand that within minutes of this Status Conference being over, the matter should be available for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I can only hope so. Now, I'm sorry, I should have taken your appearance. Do you want to announce it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I can guarantee that I'm here. There is almost nothing that the Defence asks for. I make the offer to my learned friend, who is otherwise engaged, if he wants me to amend the indictment on his behalf, I'm perfectly willing to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But, Mr. Morrison, the one thing that does concern me is that the form of discovery should continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have there been any problems about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's wonderful to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: No. We are -- at the moment, I don't anticipate any procedural problems between the Defence and the Prosecution, or substantive problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I ask you a question? Having read the motion, or a great proportion of it, and having read an article that you wrote recently in an English magazine, I was wondering whether you are the author of both?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You have very different styles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, it's horses for courses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Because frankly, it's a very difficult -- it's very densely expressed some of this. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: It is. And one of the problems is, to be frank, that -- I appreciate I went over the limits. Actually when you look at the motion, I only went over the limits of five pages of the actual substance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not worried about the length of it. I'm worried about the style in which it's expressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's trying to cram as much into as short a space as possible, and that's one of the problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm afraid that some of us supported that amendment 22 to that practice note and others didn't. I sometimes wonder whether there are more disadvantages than advantages. However, I perhaps should not have inquired, but the style was so different, I thought it may have been different people who had written each.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: In a sense it probably was. One was pretending to be a journalist and one was pretending to be a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Are there any matters under the rule that you want to raise in relation to your client's well-being?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: No, at the moment there aren't any significant difficulties. The only thing that I would ask, and this is a matter of practicalities, if there were to be an appeal which lies of right as far as either party is concerned under Rule 72(B)(i), there is 15 days from the date of the judgement being entered. Now, we are approaching a time when I know, for instance, that I'm going to be in Tanzania. I know my learned friend is under very considerable pressure and we are also approaching the time when the Tribunal will be closing down. So it's all I ask for is if the date for judgement is possible to indicate before the actual date the judgement is delivered the date or a date on which it may be delivered, it would be of enormous assistance

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I can assure you that we have had other things on our plates as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But nevertheless, hopefully, it will be out before the vacation, but we can grant you leave, an extension of time, I think. I'm not altogether satisfied that it is within the appeal as a right because it has been altered now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, I know I was waiting to see whether anybody was going do raise that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I only say to you, I'm not sure. I haven't really considered it and it's not a matter for me to consider but it's interesting because unless it goes to jurisdiction, you have to get leave. So if I were you, I would try a belt and braces approach myself and do each in the alternative but you will certainly be given fair warning of when we propose to deliver the decision. If we do have power to grant you an extension of time, we will do so. If we don't, if necessary, we can delay its delivery until it is an appropriate time because we don't want your client to miss out in any way on his rights in relation to the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is a massive issue if I may put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: It is and the more you look into it, the bigger it gets. That's the trouble. And Your Honour will appreciate there was actually far more material available than found its way into the motion but there has to be a limitation somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, when you say material, if there are any further references that you want to give, there is no harm in you giving us a supplementary sheet of paper with the names of the cases on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I would certainly limit it to that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Because if there is one issue about which there is no common approach, this seems to be it, and some courts have not always spoken with the same voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: It's trying to find two courts which have, which is the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But I'm worried about some of the courts within themselves have not spoken with the one voice. But we would appreciate any assistance you can give, we would like to get the result right whichever way it goes. All right, then, was there anything else that we should deal with at this Status Conference? I'm very grateful to you for coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And we will adjourn.
